title: The DMA probe's zero-reachable record has more than tripled since obs-2026-08-13-2 without becoming a distinguishable pattern -- it is now a permanent-outage fact, not merely a persisting one, and the practice's own docstrings still narrate it as a single dated event
statement: obs-2026-08-13-2.json (2026-08-13) found the Danish Maritime Authority probe had answered 'reachable' on none of its four recorded attempts (2026-08-07, 2026-08-08, 2026-08-11, 2026-08-12), against darkocean/sources.py's module docstring (lines 15-17), which reads 'the source failed three probes on 2026-08-08 and is probed (never fetched) each night until it answers'. Nine nights later, autonomy/log.jsonl now carries thirteen darkocean-run entries (2026-08-07 through 2026-08-21, minus the anchor-deadlock gap on 2026-08-09/2026-08-10 that obs-2026-08-11-1.json and obs-2026-08-12-1.json already explain), and every single one still reads `"dma": "outage: URLError"` -- probe_dma (practice/src/practice/darkocean/sources.py, lines 121-131) has never once returned its other possible state, `reachable (HTTP ...)`, across the practice's entire operating life. The docstring's wording is unchanged since 2026-08-13: it still names one date (2026-08-08) and still frames the outage as something the adapter is 'probed... each night until it answers', which reads as an open question rather than the settled fact thirteen consecutive identical nights now show. darkocean/METHOD.md (line 137) carries the same framing verbatim: 'The DMA outage of 2026-08-08 stands in the record as an outage' -- a sentence that was already anchored to a single night when it was written and has not been revisited since, even as the record it describes grew to more than triple its 2026-08-13 length.
method: python3 -c "import json; [print(json.loads(l)['detail'].get('date'), json.loads(l)['detail'].get('dma')) for l in open('autonomy/log.jsonl') if json.loads(l).get('step')=='darkocean-run']" -- read every darkocean-run entry's dma field directly, same method as obs-2026-08-13-2.json extended to the full log. Re-read darkocean/sources.py's module docstring, DMA_NOTE (lines 35-37) and probe_dma (lines 121-131), and darkocean/METHOD.md's DMA row and failures paragraph (lines 135-139), to check whether either had been revised in the nine nights since the prior observation.
worth_watching_because: obs-2026-08-13-2.json declined to propose a sensor for this pattern because, with every recorded night identical, a threshold or N-consecutive-nights rule would have nothing to distinguish -- and that reasoning still holds tonight: thirteen identical nights distinguish no better than four did, since the sensor would fire on the same single fact either way. What has changed is not the shape of the evidence but its weight: at four nights the outage could plausibly still be the 2026-08-08 incident the docstring names, not yet resolved; at thirteen nights spanning the practice's entire recorded life, with the anchor-deadlock gap the only interruption, 'the source failed three probes on 2026-08-08' is no longer a fair paraphrase of the record -- it reads as a bounded, dated incident when the committed fact is that this source has never once answered. Re-checked tonight rather than left for a future pass because obs-2026-08-13-2.json's own left_alone clause named a condition for revisiting this ('if DMA answers even once and then stops again') that has not occurred, but did not anticipate the alternative that actually happened: the same unbroken outage simply continuing to grow past the point where the docstring's framing stays accurate.
left_alone: Still not proposing a sensor, for the same reason obs-2026-08-13-2.json gave: a single probed-only source with every recorded night identical gives a threshold nothing to distinguish. What this observation does change from its predecessor: the docstring and METHOD.md wording were narrative-accuracy questions on 2026-08-13, with three nights of slack between what they said and what the record showed; at thirteen consecutive nights the gap between 'failed three probes on 2026-08-08' and 'has not answered on any recorded night since' is wide enough that leaving the wording as-is would let a reader underestimate the outage's duration by a factor of three or more. Corrected tonight (practice/src/practice/darkocean/sources.py's module docstring and DMA_NOTE, darkocean/METHOD.md's failures paragraph) to describe the outage as ongoing since first probed rather than anchored to one date, without inventing a claim the record doesn't support (still not asserting anything about DMA's service itself, only about how long this observatory's own probe has gone unanswered) and without hardcoding today's date in its place, so the correction does not itself go stale the same way.
